Option <tt>RTCLOCK</tt>. * Leds. Option <tt>LEDS</tt>. * Power transistors. Option <tt>TRANSISTORS</tt>. * Switches and user button. Option <tt>SWITCHES</tt>. * RS232 serial interface. Option <tt>RS232</tt>. IRQ for RS232 can be enabled with <tt>RS232_IRQ_SUPPORT</tt>. * HV7131GP Camera. Option <tt>CAMERA</tt>. IRQ for the Ethernet can be enabled with <tt>ETHERNET_IRQ_SUPPORT</tt>. Please note that ZigBee and Ethernet are mutually exclusive. * Everything, included the ZigBee (Ethernet is excluded). Option <tt>ALL_ZIGBEE</tt>. * Everything, included the Ethernet (ZigBee is excluded). Option <tt>ALL_ETHERNET</tt>.

page.title: Lauterbach TRACE32 Support for Infineon Aurix

revision.comment: Created page with "The ERIKA build system for Infineon AURIX produces a Lauterbach Trace32 configuration file ('''t32.cmm''') and a ORTI description file ('''system.orti''') inside the output direc..."
revision.text:
The ERIKA build system for Infineon AURIX produces a Lauterbach Trace32 configuration file ('''t32.cmm''') and a ORTI description file ('''system.orti''') inside the output directory. The ORTI file is produced only if ORTI support is enabled in the OIL configuration file. To launch the Trace32 debugger for singlecore projects, please issue '''t32mtc''' from the output directory. The ERIKA build system honors the '''T32SYS''' environment variable, if set (default ''T32SYS ?= C:/T32'')
=== Muticore Projects ===
For multicore projects, the files mentioned above are produced inside the core directories for each core, and a startup script (named '''tc27x_mc_start.sh''' under cygwin and linux or '''tc27x_mc_start.bat''' for Windows cmd) is produced in the output directory. If the build targeted AURIX Flash (the default behaviour), before executing debug you need to flash multicore images. To do that simply execute '''tc27x_mc_flash.sh''' (under Linux or Cygwin environment) or '''tc27x_mc_flash.bat''' (in Windows environment) scripts.
To run the debugger, please issue ''tc27x_mc_start.[sh,bat]'' from the output directory. The script creates up to three instances of the debugger, one for each core. Slave cores cannot be started until master core (Core 0) enable them, thing that is made early in start-up code. Nonetheless, the startup script loads all the code and the debug symbols for each core and each debugger instances. The barrier inside '''StartOS()''' comes handy to synchronize the code running on the different cores.
'''N.B.''' To let know the build system for wich Trace32 architecture (windows, windows64, pc_linux ecc.) it have to generate script for, set '''T32ARCH''' environment variable/pass it as make parameter with the right value (default ''T32ARCH ?= windows64'').

page.title: Lauterbach TRACE32 Support for Leopard MPC5643L

revision.comment: Created page with "The reference debugging solution for MPC5643L is Lauterbach. In the Erika tree (look at pkg/mcu/freescale_mpc5643l/cfg) is collected a set of Lauterbach sripts for single and mul..."
revision.text: The reference debugging solution for MPC5643L is Lauterbach. In the Erika tree (look at pkg/mcu/freescale_mpc5643l/cfg) is collected a set of Lauterbach sripts for single and multicore configurations. Such a scripts also provide support for execution from SRAM and Flash, in VLE and BookE mode. MPC5643L provides the capability to work in lock-step mode, for this reason a script to pass from/to DPM/lock-step mode is provide (set_lsm_dpm.cmm). To launch this script, user have to launch Lauterbach Tracer first (for instance by editing "t32mppc" in Linux prompt, or equivalent command under Window), and then editing "do set_lsm_dpm.cmm" in the Lauterbach command prompt. This script provides several functionalities, but the only functionality addressed by this manual is the one to switch from/to lock-step/DPM mode. Once the user launches this script the following window appears: [[Image:set_lock_step.png]] Red box shows two buttons to select lock-step or DPM mode. For instance, in this case we have a system set as DPM, if we would like to switch to LSM mode, we have to press the LSM button, and then press "PROGRAM". After this action, a confirmation window will be shown, press "YES" to confirm: [[Image:lock_step_ok_button.png]] If the programming task is successfully accomplished, the following window will be shown. Press "OK" to terminate the script. [[Image:lock_step_ok_message.png]] IMPORTANT NOTE: in order to make the switch-mode effective, a power-cycle has to be done. Therefore power your board off, and then power it on.

page.title: MONOSTACK - writing the monostack part of a CPU layer

revision.text: === Description === The following steps explain how to write the MONOSTACK part of a CPU layer.

=== Description ===
Monostack Hardware Abstraction Layer: All the threads and the interrupts share the same stack. That kind of HAL can only be used if the scheduling algorithm used by the Kernel Layer guarantees that a preempted thread cannot execute again before all the preempter threads have finished their instances.
* The following steps explain how to write the MONOSTACK part of a CPU layer.

The Monostack configuration of the ERIKA Kernel models the fact that all tasks and ISRs in the system share the same stack.
This stack configuraton can only be used when the scheduling algorithm implemented by the kernel insures that there is not an interleaving among the various tasks in the system.
That is, the kernel must guarantee that there are no blocking primitives implemented in the system. OSEK/VDX Immediate Priority Ceiling Protocol guarantees that property.
The Monostack configuration has some nice properties, in particular due to the fact that, in the FP, EDF, and FRSH kernels, there is no need to save registers when a context switch happens because a task called a primitive.

That is, the kernel must guarantee that there are no blocking primitives implemented in the system. OSEK/VDX Immediate Priority Ceiling Protocol guarantees that property.
The Monostack configuration has some nice properties, in particular due to the fact that, in the FP, EDF, and FRSH kernels, there is no need to save registers when a context switch happens because a task called a primitive.

page.title: MULTISTACK - writing the multistack part of a CPU layer

revision.text:
=== Description ===
Multistack HAL: Every thread can have its private stack, or it can share it with other threads. This allows the Kernel Layer to use scheduling algorithms that could block threads in synchronization primitives (as for example, a fixed priority scheduler with semaphores) or for arbitrary reasons (as, for example, a classical round robin scheduler).
* The following steps explain how to write the MULTISTACK part of a CPU layer.

In the Multistack HAL every thread can have its private stack, or it can share it with other threads. This allows the Kernel Layer to use scheduling algorithms that could block threads in synchronization primitives (as for example, a fixed priority scheduler with semaphores) or for arbitrary reasons (as, for example, a classical round robin scheduler).
Some code required for Multistack is already available in among the [[Common files for the HAL]]. This is used for example in the [[PPC e200]] or the [[Lattice Mico32]] ports. Those ports feature a HAL that is easier to write than older ports, so you are encouraged to take those ports as a reference to develop your new port.

= U-Boot =
== U-Boot for AT91RM9200DK ==
With commit number 87fee013a23ad02821699aef5b76891b42959182, Linux developers removed the default mach type for at91rm9200 boards, in order to make developers fix buggy bootloaders.
Thus, current versions of U-Boot cannot boot newer versions of Linux on at91rm9200dk boards. The problem is related to U-Boot, which passes a wrong mach type if compiled for the at91rm9200dk board.
This (trivial) patch makes U-Boot do its job.

== U-Boot for AT91RM9200DK ==
With commit number 87fee013a23ad02821699aef5b76891b42959182, Linux developers removed the default mach type for at91rm9200 boards, in order to make developers fix buggy bootloaders.
Thus, current versions of U-Boot cannot boot newer versions of Linux on at91rm9200dk boards. The problem is related to U-Boot, which passes a wrong mach type if compiled for the at91rm9200dk board.
This (trivial) patch makes U-Boot do its job.

>From 1a828b63fea0755df232eb27993bf69370674473 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: Claudio Scordino <claudio@evidence.eu.com> Date: Wed, 27 Aug 2008 12:04:44 +0200 Subject: [PATCH 1/1] Fix MACH_TYPE for the AT91RM9200DK board.
Signed-off-by: Claudio Scordino <claudio@evidence.eu.com> --- board/atmel/at91rm9200dk/at91rm9200dk.c | 2 +- 1 files changed, 1 insertions(+), 1 deletions(-)
diff --git a/board/atmel/at91rm9200dk/at91rm9200dk.c b/board/atmel/at91rm9200dk/at91rm9200dk.c index c564f73..b89a3fd 100644 --- a/board/atmel/at91rm9200dk/at91rm9200dk.c +++ b/board/atmel/at91rm9200dk/at91rm9200dk.c @@ -47,7 +47,7 @@ int board_init (void) /* so we do _nothing_ here */
/* arch number of AT91RM9200DK-Board */ - gd->bd->bi_arch_number = MACH_TYPE_AT91RM9200; + gd->bd->bi_arch_number = MACH_TYPE_AT91RM9200DK; /* adress of boot parameters */ gd->bd->bi_boot_params = PHYS_SDRAM + 0x100;
-- 1.5.4.3

=== Scilab/Scicos code generator for Xenomai ===
Procedure:
* Logon to the host PC (as any user) and execute the following commands: "mkdir my_dir" "cd my_dir" * Make sure that the downloaded Xenomai 2.4.3 and Linux kernel 2.6.24 are in the "my_dir" directory and subsquently execute the following commands: "tar -jxf linux-2.6.24.tar.bz2" "tar -jxf xenomai-2.4.3.tar.bz2" "cd xenomai-2.4.3" "patch -p1 -i xenomai_automata_candriver_v1.0.patch" "./scripts/prepare-kernel.sh" * Responses while preparing the kernel: Linux tree -> "~/my_dir/linux-2.6.24" Target architecture -> "i686" Adeos path -> press Enter key * After the patching has completed, execute the following commands in the same directory (xenomai-2.4.3): "./configure --prefix=xeno_dir --enable-linux-build=~/my_dir/linux-2.6.24" "cp config_linux_xenomai_automata linux/.config" "make oldconfig" "make" * Logon to the host PC (as root) and execute the following command: "make install" * Connect the host PC to the target AUTOMATA A1 via LAN. * Download the "xeno_dir" directory with the same name on the target. * Copy the boot-image file "cp ~/my_dir/linux-2.6.24/linux/arch/i386/boot/bzImage ~/my_dir/vmlinuz-2.6.24-xenomai" * Download the "~/my_dir/vmlinux-2.6.24-xenomai" file on the "/boot"directory of the target. * Download the "/lib/modules/2.6.24-xenomai" directory with the same name on the target. * Change the bootloader configuration of the target to include the "bzImage" * Restart the target and boot it with the Xenomai kernel * The Automata A1 is CAN bus ready.

At the [http://robot.unipv.it Robotics Laboratory] at the University of Pavia, Ettore Di Palma is working to the interface of the FLEX board to current sensors from [http://www.lem.com/ LEM], aiming at the wireless monitoring of electric loads. Sensors currently adopted are the [http://www.lem.com/hq/en/component/option,com_catalog/task,displayserie/serie,AT/output_type,/ AT series] components AT 100 B10 and AT 50 B10. * [[Altera Nios II]] * [[ARM7TDMI]] * [[Atmel AVR5]] * [[EnSilica eSi-RISC]] * [[Freescale S12]] * [[Infineon Tricore]] * [[Lattice Mico32]] * [[Microchip dsPIC]] (including dsPIC30, dsPIC33, and PIC24) * [[Microchip PIC32]] * [[Freescale PPC e200 (MPC 56xx)]] (including PPC e200 z0, z6, z7) * [[TI MSP430]]
Howtos * [[Porting ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid to a new microcontroller]]
Support for Hitachi H8, C167/ST10 has been moved in the "old" session since there has been not much work on them and we cannot guarantee they still compile. If interested in them just write us an e-mail!

== Supported Devices ==
This is a list of the architectures supported by ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid
* [[Altera Nios II]] * [[ARM7TDMI]] * [[Atmel AVR5]] * [[ARM Cortex M0]] * [[EnSilica eSi-RISC]] * [[Freescale PPC e200 (MPC 56xx)]] (including PPC e200 z0, z6, z7) * [[Freescale S12]] * [[Infineon Tricore]] * [[Lattice Mico32]] * [[Microchip dsPIC]] (including dsPIC30, dsPIC33, and PIC24) * [[Microchip PIC32]] * [[TI MSP430]]
Howtos * [[Porting ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid to a new microcontroller]]
Support for Hitachi H8, C167/ST10 has been moved in the "old" session since there has been not much work on them and we cannot guarantee they still compile. If interested in them just write us an e-mail!

* [[Altera Nios II]] * [[ARM7TDMI]] * [[Atmel AVR5]] * [[ARM Cortex MX]] * [[EnSilica eSi-RISC]] * [[Freescale PPC e200 (MPC 56xx)]] (including PPC e200 z0, z6, z7) * [[Freescale S12]] * [[Infineon Tricore]] * [[Lattice Mico32]] * [[Microchip dsPIC]] (including dsPIC30, dsPIC33, and PIC24) * [[Microchip PIC32]] * [[TI MSP430]]
Howtos * [[Porting ERIKA Enterprise and RT-Druid to a new microcontroller]]
Support for Hitachi H8, C167/ST10 has been moved in the "old" session since there has been not much work on them and we cannot guarantee they still compile. If interested in them just write us an e-mail!

Support for Hitachi H8, C167/ST10 has been moved in the "old" session since there has been not much work on them and we cannot guarantee they still compile. If interested in them just write us an e-mail!

ERIKA Enterprise is not an AUTOSAR RTOS. Neverthless, we are trying as much as possible to make an implementation similar to the AUTOSAR OS requirements. These pages describe the current development status.

revision.comment: Created page with "This makefile has these main targets: * download the last release of EE_RT-Druid CLI package (i.e. RT-Druid with Erika Enterprise source files) * use RT-Druid to configure the sy..."
revision.text:
This makefile has these main targets: * download the last release of EE_RT-Druid CLI package (i.e. RT-Druid with Erika Enterprise source files) * use RT-Druid to configure the system * build the system using Erika Enterprise files
<nowiki> ############################################################# # # CONVERT_PATH macro is used to get an absolute path that can # be used by host programs, like JAVA # #############################################################
ifeq ($(strip $(HOST_OS)),) HOST_OS :=$(shell uname -a) endif
# CYGWIN Specific ifeq ($(findstring CYGWIN, ${HOST_OS}), CYGWIN) # CYGWIN CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(shell cygpath -m $(1)) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(shell cygpath $(1)) else # DEFAULT (unix like) CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(1) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(1) endif
############################################################# # # Tools paths. By defaylt all paths are related to TOOLS_BASE # ############################################################# TOOLS_BASE ?= tools RTDRUID_HOME ?= $(TOOLS_BASE)/RT-Druid
# EE_TEMP should be absolute ifdef EE_TEMP EE_TEMP := $(abspath EE_TEMP) else EE_TEMP := $(abspath $(TOOLS_BASE)/temp) endif
# ERIKA_FILES should be an absolute path in the OS format, while EEBASE is in the # Makefile form and should be used only inside the makefile ifdef ERIKA_FILES export ERIKA_FILES endif
# Output folder BUILD_DIR ?= output
############################################################# # # HTTP URL of RT-Druid package. # #############################################################
# Example: tuxfamily standard path RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=EE_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= http://software.evidence.eu.com/ee_161/CLI/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
# Example: custom path with password # RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=MY_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --ask-password http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --password=123456 http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
############################################################# # # RT-Druid input files # #############################################################
# The list of input files. # Current version of makefile does not support paths and file names with whitespace # By default the input file is just "conf.oil". If the user set INPUTS_PATH, INPUTS # will contain all files with suffix .oil, .arxml and .ertd ifndef INPUTS INPUTS := conf.oil ifdef INPUTS_PATH INPUTS := $(shell find $(INPUTS_PATH) -iname "*.oil" -or -iname "*.ertd") endif else ifdef INPUTS_PATH $(error INPUTS_PATH can be specified only if INPUTS is empty or unset) endif endif
ifneq ($(notdir $(RTDRUID_HOME)),RT-Druid) $(warning RT-Druid update target works better if RTDRUID_HOME ends with RT-Druid) endif
############################################################# # # HELP # ############################################################# .PHONY: help help: @echo -e "
\ This makefile tries to setup the environment needed to build a system based on
\ RT-Druid and Erika Enterprise. The environment is downloaded and updated through
\ the web, using
\ - svn for Erikae Enterprise sources and
\ - wget for RT-Druid packages (here it is used the smallest Command Line package).
\ 
\ Please note that this makefile cannot handle paths and filenames with whitespaces
\ 
\ Targets:
\ update_ee_rtduid - updates RT-Druid packages and Erika Enterprise.
\ configure - using RT-Druid, configure an Erika Enterprise system.
\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_ee_rtduid.
\ build - build the configurated system.
\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_ee_rtduid.
\ build_clean - clean the results of a build process, without touch the generated
\ configuration.
\ all - calls build_clean and build targets.
\ Considering all dependecies, the result is:
\ * tries to clean an existing build (all errors are ignored);
\ * check if RT-Druid is available; if not, download a new one;
\ * check if configuration folder exist and is newer than RT-Druid
\ folder; if not, runs RT-Druid to generate the new configuration
\ * build the system
\ 
\ Variables:
\ TOOLS_BASE - path used to build default values of RT-Druid, Erika Enterprise
\ and temp folders.
\ (current value = $(TOOLS_BASE) )
\ RTDRUID_HOME - path of RT-Druid package. It should end with RT-Druid.
\ Default TOOL_BASE/RT-Druid
\ (current value = $(RTDRUID_HOME) )
\ ERIKA_FILES - even if discouraged, it can be used to select a different path of
\ Erika Enterprise sources. This path has to be in the host format,
\ i.e. all absolute path are like C:\ee under windows, and like
\ /opt/ee otherwise ( usually relative paths are the same in both
\ windows and linux).
\ By default is unset and RT-Druid points to erika enterprise files
\ inside RT-Druid plugins
\ (current value = $(ERIKA_FILES) )
\ EE_TEMP - path of a folder used to save bakups and temporary files used to
\ correctly do RT-Druid updates. Default TOOL_BASE/temp
\ (current value = $(EE_TEMP) )
\ BUILD_DIR - the path where RT-Druid will place the folder with all generated
\ configuration files.
\ (current value = $(BUILD_DIR) )
\ INPUTS - list of files (spaced by a whitespace) used by RT-Druid as input
\ for configuration generation process.
\ Default conf.oil
\ (current value = $(INPUTS) )

ifeq ($(strip $(HOST_OS)),) HOST_OS :=$(shell uname -a) endif
# CYGWIN Specific ifeq ($(findstring CYGWIN, ${HOST_OS}), CYGWIN) # CYGWIN CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(shell cygpath -m $(1)) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(shell cygpath $(1)) else # DEFAULT (unix like) CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(1) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(1) endif
############################################################# # # Tools paths. By defaylt all paths are related to TOOLS_BASE # ############################################################# TOOLS_BASE ?= tools RTDRUID_HOME ?= $(TOOLS_BASE)/RT-Druid
# EE_TEMP should be absolute ifdef EE_TEMP EE_TEMP := $(abspath EE_TEMP) else EE_TEMP := $(abspath $(TOOLS_BASE)/temp) endif
# ERIKA_FILES should be an absolute path in the OS format, while EEBASE is in the # Makefile form and should be used only inside the makefile ifdef ERIKA_FILES export ERIKA_FILES endif
# Output folder BUILD_DIR ?= output
############################################################# # # HTTP URL of RT-Druid package. # #############################################################
# Example: tuxfamily standard path RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=EE_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= http://software.evidence.eu.com/ee_161/CLI/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
# Example: custom path with password # RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=MY_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --ask-password http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --password=123456 http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
############################################################# # # RT-Druid input files # #############################################################
# The list of input files. # Current version of makefile does not support paths and file names with whitespace # By default the input file is just "conf.oil". If the user set INPUTS_PATH, INPUTS # will contain all files with suffix .oil, .arxml and .ertd ifndef INPUTS INPUTS := conf.oil ifdef INPUTS_PATH INPUTS := $(shell find $(INPUTS_PATH) -iname "*.oil" -or -iname "*.ertd") endif else ifdef INPUTS_PATH $(error INPUTS_PATH can be specified only if INPUTS is empty or unset) endif endif
ifneq ($(notdir $(RTDRUID_HOME)),RT-Druid) $(warning RT-Druid update target works better if RTDRUID_HOME ends with RT-Druid) endif

\ This makefile tries to setup the environment needed to build a system based on

The suggestion is to set TOOLS_BASE in the environment before run the makefile. Examples: * TOOLS_BASE=C:/Evidence/ * TOOLS_BASE=$HOME/Evidence

<nowiki> ############################################################# # # CONVERT_PATH macro is used to get an absolute path that can # be used by host programs, like JAVA # #############################################################
ifeq ($(strip $(HOST_OS)),) HOST_OS :=$(shell uname -a) endif
# CYGWIN Specific ifeq ($(findstring CYGWIN, ${HOST_OS}), CYGWIN) # CYGWIN CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(shell cygpath -m $(1)) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(shell cygpath $(1)) else # DEFAULT (unix like) CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(1) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(1) endif
############################################################# # # Tools paths. By defaylt all paths are related to TOOLS_BASE # ############################################################# TOOLS_BASE ?= tools RTDRUID_HOME ?= $(TOOLS_BASE)/RT-Druid
# EE_TEMP should be absolute ifdef EE_TEMP EE_TEMP := $(abspath EE_TEMP) else EE_TEMP := $(abspath $(TOOLS_BASE)/temp) endif
# ERIKA_FILES should be an absolute path in the OS format, while EEBASE is in the # Makefile form and should be used only inside the makefile ifdef ERIKA_FILES export ERIKA_FILES endif
# Output folder BUILD_DIR ?= output
############################################################# # # HTTP URL of RT-Druid package. # #############################################################
# Example: tuxfamily standard path RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=EE_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= http://software.evidence.eu.com/ee_161/CLI/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
# Example: custom path with password # RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=MY_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --ask-password http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --password=123456 http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
############################################################# # # RT-Druid input files # #############################################################
# The list of input files. # Current version of makefile does not support paths and file names with whitespace # By default the input file is just "conf.oil". If the user set INPUTS_PATH, INPUTS # will contain all files with suffix .oil, .arxml and .ertd ifndef INPUTS INPUTS := conf.oil ifdef INPUTS_PATH INPUTS := $(shell find $(INPUTS_PATH) -iname "*.oil" -or -iname "*.ertd") endif else ifdef INPUTS_PATH $(error INPUTS_PATH can be specified only if INPUTS is empty or unset) endif endif
ifneq ($(notdir $(RTDRUID_HOME)),RT-Druid) $(warning RT-Druid update target works better if RTDRUID_HOME ends with RT-Druid) endif

\ This makefile tries to setup the environment needed to build a system based on
\ RT-Druid and Erika Enterprise. The environment is downloaded and updated through
\ the web, using
\ - svn for Erikae Enterprise sources and
\ - wget for RT-Druid packages (here it is used the smallest Command Line package).
\ 
\ Please note that this makefile cannot handle paths and filenames with whitespaces
\ 
\ Targets:
\ update_ee_rtduid - updates RT-Druid packages and Erika Enterprise.
\ configure - using RT-Druid, configure an Erika Enterprise system.
\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_ee_rtduid.
\ build - build the configurated system.
\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_ee_rtduid.
\ build_clean - clean the results of a build process, without touch the generated
\ configuration.
\ all - calls build_clean and build targets.
\ Considering all dependecies, the result is:
\ * tries to clean an existing build (all errors are ignored);
\ * check if RT-Druid is available; if not, download a new one;

\ folder; if not, runs RT-Druid to generate the new configuration
\ * build the system
\ 
\ Variables:
\ TOOLS_BASE - path used to build default values of RT-Druid, Erika Enterprise
\ and temp folders.

\ RTDRUID_HOME - path of RT-Druid package. It should end with RT-Druid.

\ (current value = $(EE_TEMP) )
\ BUILD_DIR - the path where RT-Druid will place the folder with all generated
\ configuration files.
\ (current value = $(BUILD_DIR) )
\ INPUTS - list of files (spaced by a whitespace) used by RT-Druid as input

\ INPUTS_PATH - identifies one or more folders (spaced by a whitespace) where look

revision.text:
This makefile has these main targets: * checkout or update Erika Enterprise from svn * download the last release of RT-Druid CLI package * use RT-Druid to configure the system * build the system using Erika Enterprise files
<nowiki> ############################################################# # # CONVERT_PATH macro is used to get an absolute path that can # be used by host programs, like JAVA # #############################################################
ifeq ($(strip $(HOST_OS)),) HOST_OS :=$(shell uname -a) endif
# CYGWIN Specific ifeq ($(findstring CYGWIN, ${HOST_OS}), CYGWIN) # CYGWIN CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(shell cygpath -m $(1)) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(shell cygpath $(1)) else # DEFAULT (unix like) CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(1) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(1) endif
############################################################# # # Tools paths. By defaylt all paths are related to TOOLS_BASE # ############################################################# TOOLS_BASE ?= tools RTDRUID_HOME ?= $(TOOLS_BASE)/RT-Druid
# EE_TEMP should be absolute ifdef EE_TEMP EE_TEMP := $(abspath EE_TEMP) else EE_TEMP := $(abspath $(TOOLS_BASE)/temp) endif
# ERIKA_FILES should be an absolute path in the OS format, while EEBASE is in the # Makefile form and should be used only inside the makefile ifdef EEBASE $(warning EEBASE is already defined and will be override. Use ERIKA_FILES instead) endif
ifndef ERIKA_FILES ERIKA_FILES := $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS,$(TOOLS_BASE)/ee) endif EEBASE := $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK,$(ERIKA_FILES)) ERIKA_FILES := $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS, $(abspath $(EEBASE))) # export ERIKA_FILES because it is used by RT-Druid export ERIKA_FILES
# Output folder BUILD_DIR ?= output
############################################################# # # HTTP URL of RT-Druid package. # #############################################################
# Example: tuxfamily standard path RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= http://software.evidence.eu.com/ee_161/CLI/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
# Example: custom path with password # RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=MY_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --ask-password http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --password=123456 http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
############################################################# # # RT-Druid input files # #############################################################
# The list of input files. # Current version of makefile does not support paths and file names with whitespace # By default the input file is just "conf.oil". If the user set INPUTS_PATH, INPUTS # will contain all files with suffix .oil, .arxml and .ertd ifndef INPUTS INPUTS := conf.oil ifdef INPUTS_PATH INPUTS := $(shell find $(INPUTS_PATH) -iname "*.oil" -or -iname "*.ertd") endif else ifdef INPUTS_PATH $(error INPUTS_PATH can be specified only if INPUTS is empty or unset) endif endif
ifneq ($(notdir $(RTDRUID_HOME)),RT-Druid) $(warning RT-Druid update target works better if RTDRUID_HOME ends with RT-Druid) endif
############################################################# # # HELP # ############################################################# .PHONY: help help: @echo -e "
\ This makefile tries to setup the environment needed to build a system based on
\ RT-Druid and Erika Enterprise. The environment is downloaded and updated through
\ the web, using
\ - svn for Erikae Enterprise sources and
\ - wget for RT-Druid packages (here it is used the smallest Command Line package).
\ 
\ Please note that this makefile cannot handle paths and filenames with whitespaces
\ 
\ Targets:
\ update_erika - updates Erika Enterprise to the latest version in the svn.
\ update_rtduid - updates RT-Druid packages.
\ configure - using RT-Druid, configure an Erika Enterprise system.
\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_rtduid.
\ build - build the configurated system
\ Depends on ERIKA_FILES and may call update_erika.
\ build_clean - clean the results of a build process, without touch the generated
\ configuration.
\ all - calls build_clean and build targets.
\ Considering all dependecies, the result is:
\ * tries to clean an existing build (all errors are ignored);
\ * check if RT-Druid is available; if not, download a new one;
\ * check if configuration folder exist and is newer than RT-Druid
\ folder; if not, runs RT-Druid to generate the new configuration
\ * check if Erika Enterprise source folder exist; if not, download
\ a new one;
\ * build the system
\ 
\ Variables:
\ TOOLS_BASE - path used to build default values of RT-Druid, Erika Enterprise
\ and temp folders.
\ (current value = $(TOOLS_BASE) )
\ RTDRUID_HOME - path of RT-Druid package. It should end with RT-Druid.
\ Default TOOL_BASE/RT-Druid
\ (current value = $(RTDRUID_HOME) )
\ ERIKA_FILES - path of Erika Enterprise sources. This path has to be in the host
\ format, i.e. all absolute path are like C:\ee under windows, and
\ like /opt/ee otherwise (usually relative paths are the same in
\ both windows and linux).
\ Default TOOL_BASE/ee (converted to host path if needed)
\ (current value = $(ERIKA_FILES) )
\ EE_TEMP - path of a folder used to save bakups and temporary files used to
\ correctly do RT-Druid updates. Default TOOL_BASE/temp
\ (current value = $(EE_TEMP) )
\ BUILD_DIR - the path where RT-Druid will place the folder with all generated
\ configuration files.
\ (current value = $(BUILD_DIR) )
\ INPUTS - list of files (spaced by a whitespace) used by RT-Druid as input
\ for configuration generation process.
\ Default conf.oil
\ (current value = $(INPUTS) )
\ INPUTS_PATH - identifies one or more folders (spaced by a whitespace) where look
\ for RT-Druid input files. This variable cannnot be used if INPUTS
\ is set.
\ (current value = $(INPUTS_PATH) )
\ 
\ Examples:
\ make all
\ TOOLS_BASE=/opt/evidence make all
\ TOOLS_BASE=/opt/evidence INPUTS_PATH=conf make build
\ INPUTS=\`ls --format=horizontal conf/*\` make build
\ INPUTS=\`find conf -type f -printf "%p "\` make build"
############################################################# # # Update Erika Enterprise # ############################################################# .PHONY: update_erika update_erika $(EEBASE): @mkdir -p $(EE_TEMP) ; \ if [ -d "$(EEBASE)" ]; \ then ( \ echo -e "\ =================================
\ Update Erika Enterprise
\ =================================" ;\ rm -f $(EE_TEMP)/ee_checkout.log ;\ cd $(EEBASE); svn update \ ) else (\ echo -e "\ =================================
\ Checkout Erika Enterprise
\ =================================" ;\ rm -f $(EE_TEMP)/ee_checkout.log ;\ svn checkout svn://svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee $(EEBASE) \ ) \ fi
############################################################# # # Update RT-Druid # ############################################################# .PHONY: update_rtdruid update_rtdruid: download_rtdruid $(RTDRUID_HOME)
download_rtdruid $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME): @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Update RT-Druid
\ =================================" @mkdir -p $(EE_TEMP) ; \ cd $(EE_TEMP) ; wget -N $(RTDRUID_WEB_SITE)
$(RTDRUID_HOME): $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) @if [ -d "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" ]; then (\ cp "$(RTDRUID_HOME)/configuration/common_oil.pref" $(EE_TEMP) 2>/dev/null ;\ rm -rf "$(EE_TEMP)/RT-Druid_backup"; \ mv "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" "$(EE_TEMP)/RT-Druid_backup" && \ rm -rf $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ ) fi && \ unzip $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) -d $(TOOLS_BASE) && \ (cp "$(EE_TEMP)/common_oil.pref" "$(RTDRUID_HOME)/configuration/" 2>/dev/null || exit 0); \ if [ -d "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" ]; then (\ touch $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ ) else ( \ echo "RT-Druid HOME does not exist. Check zip file and RTDRUID_HOME"; exit 1 \ ) fi
############################################################# # # Use RT-Druid to configure Erika Enterprise # ############################################################# .PHONY: configure configure $(BUILD_DIR): $(RTDRUID_HOME) $(INPUTS) @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Configure
\ =================================" @bash $(RTDRUID_HOME)/evidence/generate_code.sh \ $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS, $(INPUTS)) \ $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS, $(BUILD_DIR)) && \ (if [ -d "$(BUILD_DIR)" ]; then \ touch $(BUILD_DIR) ; \ else \ echo "System configured but $(BUILD_DIR) does not exist" ; exit 1 ; \ fi)
############################################################# # # Compile the system # ############################################################# .PHONY: build build: $(BUILD_DIR) $(EEBASE) @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Build
\ =================================" cd $(BUILD_DIR) ; \ make
############################################################# # # Clean compile results # ############################################################# .PHONY: build_clean build_clean: $(EEBASE) @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Build Clean
\ =================================" @rm -f $(BUILD_DIR)/build.log @if [ -d "$(BUILD_DIR)" ]; then cd $(BUILD_DIR) && make clean ; fi
############################################################# # # Clean Erika Enterprise configuration files generated by # RT-Druid # ############################################################# .PHONY: conf_clean conf_clean: @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Configuration clean
\ =================================" @rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)
############################################################# # # Clean prervious compile results and do a new build # ############################################################# .PHONY: all all: build_clean build</nowiki>

\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_rtduid.
\ build - build the configurated system
\ Depends on ERIKA_FILES and may call update_erika.
\ build_clean - clean the results of a build process, without touch the generated
\ configuration.
\ all - calls build_clean and build targets.
\ Considering all dependecies, the result is:
\ * tries to clean an existing build (all errors are ignored);
\ * check if RT-Druid is available; if not, download a new one;
\ * check if configuration folder exist and is newer than RT-Druid
\ folder; if not, runs RT-Druid to generate the new configuration
\ * check if Erika Enterprise source folder exist; if not, download
\ a new one;
\ * build the system
\ 
\ Variables:
\ TOOLS_BASE - path used to build default values of RT-Druid, Erika Enterprise
\ and temp folders.
\ (current value = $(TOOLS_BASE) )
\ RTDRUID_HOME - path of RT-Druid package. It should end with RT-Druid.
\ Default TOOL_BASE/RT-Druid
\ (current value = $(RTDRUID_HOME) )
\ ERIKA_FILES - path of Erika Enterprise sources. This path has to be in the host
\ format, i.e. all absolute path are like C:\ee under windows, and
\ like /opt/ee otherwise (usually relative paths are the same in
\ both windows and linux).
\ Default TOOL_BASE/ee (converted to host path if needed)
\ (current value = $(ERIKA_FILES) )
\ EE_TEMP - path of a folder used to save bakups and temporary files used to
\ correctly do RT-Druid updates. Default TOOL_BASE/temp
\ (current value = $(EE_TEMP) )
\ BUILD_DIR - the path where RT-Druid will place the folder with all generated
\ configuration files.
\ (current value = $(BUILD_DIR) )
\ INPUTS - list of files (spaced by a whitespace) used by RT-Druid as input
\ for configuration generation process.
\ Default conf.oil
\ (current value = $(INPUTS) )
\ INPUTS_PATH - identifies one or more folders (spaced by a whitespace) where look
\ for RT-Druid input files. This variable cannnot be used if INPUTS
\ is set.
\ (current value = $(INPUTS_PATH) )
\ 
\ Examples:
\ make all
\ TOOLS_BASE=/opt/evidence make all
\ TOOLS_BASE=/opt/evidence INPUTS_PATH=conf make build
\ INPUTS=\`ls --format=horizontal conf/*\` make build
\ INPUTS=\`find conf -type f -printf "%p "\` make build"

\ =================================" ;\ rm -f $(EE_TEMP)/ee_checkout.log ;\ cd $(EEBASE); svn update \ ) else (\ echo -e "\ =================================
\ Checkout Erika Enterprise
\ =================================" ;\ rm -f $(EE_TEMP)/ee_checkout.log ;\ svn checkout svn://svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee $(EEBASE) \ ) \ fi
############################################################# # # Update RT-Druid # ############################################################# .PHONY: update_rtdruid update_rtdruid: download_rtdruid $(RTDRUID_HOME)
download_rtdruid $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME): @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Update RT-Druid
\ =================================" @mkdir -p $(EE_TEMP) ; \ cd $(EE_TEMP) ; wget -N $(RTDRUID_WEB_SITE)
$(RTDRUID_HOME): $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) @if [ -d "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" ]; then (\ cp "$(RTDRUID_HOME)/configuration/common_oil.pref" $(EE_TEMP) 2>/dev/null ;\ rm -rf "$(EE_TEMP)/RT-Druid_backup"; \ mv "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" "$(EE_TEMP)/RT-Druid_backup" && \ rm -rf $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ ) fi && \ unzip $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) -d $(TOOLS_BASE) && \ (cp "$(EE_TEMP)/common_oil.pref" "$(RTDRUID_HOME)/configuration/" 2>/dev/null || exit 0); \ if [ -d "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" ]; then (\ touch $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ ) else ( \ echo "RT-Druid HOME does not exist. The suggestion is to set TOOLS_BASE in the environment before run the makefile. Examples: * TOOLS_BASE=C:/Evidence/ * TOOLS_BASE=$HOME/Evidence

<nowiki> ############################################################# # # CONVERT_PATH macro is used to get an absolute path that can # be used by host programs, like JAVA # #############################################################
ifeq ($(strip $(HOST_OS)),) HOST_OS :=$(shell uname -a) endif
# CYGWIN Specific ifeq ($(findstring CYGWIN, ${HOST_OS}), CYGWIN) # CYGWIN CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(shell cygpath -m $(1)) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(shell cygpath $(1)) else # DEFAULT (unix like) CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS = $(1) CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK = $(1) endif
############################################################# # # Tools paths. By defaylt all paths are related to TOOLS_BASE # ############################################################# TOOLS_BASE ?= tools RTDRUID_HOME ?= $(TOOLS_BASE)/RT-Druid
# EE_TEMP should be absolute ifdef EE_TEMP EE_TEMP := $(abspath EE_TEMP) else EE_TEMP := $(abspath $(TOOLS_BASE)/temp) endif
# ERIKA_FILES should be an absolute path in the OS format, while EEBASE is in the # Makefile form and should be used only inside the makefile ifdef EEBASE $(warning EEBASE is already defined and will be override. Use ERIKA_FILES instead) endif
ifndef ERIKA_FILES ERIKA_FILES := $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS,$(TOOLS_BASE)/ee) endif EEBASE := $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_MK,$(ERIKA_FILES)) ERIKA_FILES := $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS, $(abspath $(EEBASE))) # export ERIKA_FILES because it is used by RT-Druid export ERIKA_FILES
# Output folder BUILD_DIR ?= output
############################################################# # # HTTP URL of RT-Druid package. # #############################################################
# Example: tuxfamily standard path RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= http://software.evidence.eu.com/ee_161/CLI/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
# Example: custom path with password # RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=MY_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --ask-password http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --password=123456 http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
############################################################# # # RT-Druid input files # #############################################################
# The list of input files. # Current version of makefile does not support paths and file names with whitespace # By default the input file is just "conf.oil". If the user set INPUTS_PATH, INPUTS # will contain all files with suffix .oil, .arxml and .ertd ifndef INPUTS INPUTS := conf.oil ifdef INPUTS_PATH INPUTS := $(shell find $(INPUTS_PATH) -iname "*.oil" -or -iname "*.ertd") endif else ifdef INPUTS_PATH $(error INPUTS_PATH can be specified only if INPUTS is empty or unset) endif endif
ifneq ($(notdir $(RTDRUID_HOME)),RT-Druid) $(warning RT-Druid update target works better if RTDRUID_HOME ends with RT-Druid) endif

# Example: tuxfamily standard path RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= http://software.evidence.eu.com/ee_161/CLI/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
# Example: custom path with password # RTDRUID_FILE_NAME ?=MY_RT-Druid_1.6.1.zip # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --ask-password http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) # RTDRUID_WEB_SITE ?= --user=MyUser --password=123456 http://software.evidence.eu.com/special_edition/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME)
############################################################# # # RT-Druid input files # #############################################################
# The list of input files. # Current version of makefile does not support paths and file names with whitespace # By default the input file is just "conf.oil". If the user set INPUTS_PATH, INPUTS # will contain all files with suffix .oil, .arxml and .ertd ifndef INPUTS INPUTS := conf.oil ifdef INPUTS_PATH INPUTS := $(shell find $(INPUTS_PATH) -iname "*.oil" -or -iname "*.ertd") endif else ifdef INPUTS_PATH $(error INPUTS_PATH can be specified only if INPUTS is empty or unset) endif endif
ifneq ($(notdir $(RTDRUID_HOME)),RT-Druid) $(warning RT-Druid update target works better if RTDRUID_HOME ends with RT-Druid) endif
############################################################# # # HELP # ############################################################# .PHONY: help help: @echo -e "
\ This makefile tries to setup the environment needed to build a system based on
\ RT-Druid and Erika Enterprise. The environment is downloaded and updated through
\ the web, using
\ - svn for Erikae Enterprise sources and
\ - wget for RT-Druid packages (here it is used the smallest Command Line package).
\ 
\ Please note that this makefile cannot handle paths and filenames with whitespaces
\ 
\ Targets:
\ update_erika - updates Erika Enterprise to the latest version in the svn.
\ update_rtduid - updates RT-Druid packages.
\ configure - using RT-Druid, configure an Erika Enterprise system.
\ Depends on RTDRUID_HOME and may call update_rtduid.
\ build - build the configurated system
\ Depends on ERIKA_FILES and may call update_erika.
\ build_clean - clean the results of a build process, without touch the generated
\ configuration.
\ all - calls build_clean and build targets.
\ Considering all dependecies, the result is:
\ * tries to clean an existing build (all errors are ignored);
\ * check if RT-Druid is available; if not, download a new one;
\ * check if configuration folder exist and is newer than RT-Druid
\ folder; if not, runs RT-Druid to generate the new configuration
\ * check if Erika Enterprise source folder exist; if not, download
\ a new one;
\ * build the system
\ 
\ Variables:
\ TOOLS_BASE - path used to build default values of RT-Druid, Erika Enterprise
\ and temp folders.
\ (current value = $(TOOLS_BASE) )
\ RTDRUID_HOME - path of RT-Druid package. It should end with RT-Druid.
\ Default TOOL_BASE/RT-Druid
\ (current value = $(RTDRUID_HOME) )
\ ERIKA_FILES - path of Erika Enterprise sources. This path has to be in the host
\ format, i.e. all absolute path are like C:\ee under windows, and
\ like /opt/ee otherwise (usually relative paths are the same in
\ both windows and linux).
\ Default TOOL_BASE/ee (converted to host path if needed)
\ (current value = $(ERIKA_FILES) )
\ EE_TEMP - path of a folder used to save bakups and temporary files used to
\ correctly do RT-Druid updates. Default TOOL_BASE/temp
\ (current value = $(EE_TEMP) )
\ BUILD_DIR - the path where RT-Druid will place the folder with all generated
\ configuration files.
\ (current value = $(BUILD_DIR) )
\ INPUTS - list of files (spaced by a whitespace) used by RT-Druid as input
\ for configuration generation process.
\ Default conf.oil
\ (current value = $(INPUTS) )
\ INPUTS_PATH - identifies one or more folders (spaced by a whitespace) where look
\ for RT-Druid input files. This variable cannnot be used if INPUTS
\ is set.
\ (current value = $(INPUTS_PATH) )
\ 
\ Examples:
\ make all
\ TOOLS_BASE=/opt/evidence make all
\ TOOLS_BASE=/opt/evidence INPUTS_PATH=conf make build
\ INPUTS=\`ls --format=horizontal conf/*\` make build
\ INPUTS=\`find conf -type f -printf "%p "\` make build"
############################################################# # # Update Erika Enterprise # ############################################################# .PHONY: update_erika update_erika $(EEBASE): @if [ -d "$(EEBASE)" ]; \ then ( \ echo -e "\ =================================
\ Update Erika Enterprise
\ =================================" ;\ cd $(EEBASE); svn update \ ) else (\ echo -e "\ =================================
\ Checkout Erika Enterprise
\ =================================" ;\ svn checkout svn://svn.tuxfamily.org/svnroot/erika/erikae/repos/ee/trunk/ee $(EEBASE) \ ) \ fi
############################################################# # # Update RT-Druid # ############################################################# .PHONY: update_rtdruid update_rtdruid: download_rtdruid $(RTDRUID_HOME)
download_rtdruid $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME): @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Update RT-Druid
\ =================================" @mkdir -p $(EE_TEMP) ; \ cd $(EE_TEMP) ; wget -N $(RTDRUID_WEB_SITE)
$(RTDRUID_HOME): $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) @if [ -d "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" ]; then (\ cp "$(RTDRUID_HOME)/configuration/common_oil.pref" $(EE_TEMP) 2>/dev/null ;\ rm -rf "$(EE_TEMP)/RT-Druid_backup"; \ mv "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" "$(EE_TEMP)/RT-Druid_backup" && \ rm -rf $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ ) fi && \ unzip $(EE_TEMP)/$(RTDRUID_FILE_NAME) -d $(TOOLS_BASE) && \ (cp "$(EE_TEMP)/common_oil.pref" "$(RTDRUID_HOME)/configuration/" 2>/dev/null || exit 0); \ if [ -d "$(RTDRUID_HOME)" ]; then (\ touch $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ ) else ( \ echo "RT-Druid HOME does not exist. Check zip file and RTDRUID_HOME"; exit 1 \ ) fi
############################################################# # # Use RT-Druid to configure Erika Enterprise # ############################################################# .PHONY: configure configure $(BUILD_DIR): $(RTDRUID_HOME) $(INPUTS) @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Configure
\ =================================" @bash $(RTDRUID_HOME)/evidence/generate_code.sh \ $(RTDRUID_HOME) \ $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS, $(INPUTS)) \ $(call CONVERT_PATH_TO_OS, $(BUILD_DIR)) && \ (if [ -d "$(BUILD_DIR)" ]; then \ touch $(BUILD_DIR) ; \ else \ echo "System configured but $(BUILD_DIR) does not exist" ; exit 1 ; \ fi)
############################################################# # # Compile the system # ############################################################# .PHONY: build build: $(BUILD_DIR) $(EEBASE) @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Build
\ =================================" cd $(BUILD_DIR) ; \ make
############################################################# # # Clean compile results # ############################################################# .PHONY: build_clean build_clean: $(EEBASE) @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Build Clean
\ =================================" @rm -f $(BUILD_DIR)/build.log @if [ -d "$(BUILD_DIR)" ]; then cd $(BUILD_DIR) && make clean ; fi
############################################################# # # Clean Erika Enterprise configuration files generated by # RT-Druid # ############################################################# .PHONY: conf_clean conf_clean: @echo -e "\ =================================
\ Configuration clean
\ =================================" @rm -rf $(BUILD_DIR)
############################################################# # # Clean prervious compile results and do a new build # ############################################################# .PHONY: all all: build_clean build</nowiki>
